summary: The biggest Solflare Packs moment was @jussy_world (76.5k followers) telling a story about a $180K Charizard pull and sell-back, ending with 'Rip your packs with your @solflare wallet'. It got 36k impressions, but it's all money-win framing, so it's good reach with an off-brand message. Collector Crypt had a busy day with a MoonPay PayBox launch (buy packs through AI chat agents, paid in USDC), and trust pain was loud: fake PSA slabs, a $600K counterfeit slab story, and nearly $1M in cards stolen in transit. Community Solflare Packs posts stayed steady and positive, and one creator explained keep / sell back / ship clearly.

sources_note: X search via the x connector, posts from 2026-11-02 09:00 UTC to 2026-11-03 09:00 UTC, 6 post searches and 1 X news search. Engagement numbers are copied from the X API at scan time. Volume figures for Collector Crypt and Courtyard come from an unverified third-party post. The $600K fake slab, Target lottery, HaloArena, Mudwater and McDonald's items are X news summaries (Grok-written). The HaloArena sellout was echoed by many near-identical explainer posts, likely a paid or coordinated campaign. Payments talk was thin: card, Apple Pay and Google Pay searches returned crypto debit card promos and trading bots, which were skipped. Restock bots (packpingnet, PokeRestockApp, TCGTRACKER), affiliate deal posts, giveaway links, resale listings, $CARDS and $zard token shills, and casino-style pack sites were skipped. The jussy_world post uses profit framing and is flagged for community follow-up, not reuse. Creators already in collector-base.csv or earlier daily files (e.g. @0x_invisible, @Xiznft, @AiFlippa, @witty_cruz) were excluded from new_creators.
